untertitel: Times and appointments on the phone: *at* half past four, *on* Thursday

grammatik.regel: *on* + day (on Tuesday), *at* + time (at half past four). *I'd like* ... is a polite way to say *I want* ... After *Can I* we use the base verb: Can I *have* a haircut?

redemittel.p2: Good morning, I'd like an appointment for a haircut, please.
Can I come *on* Thursday *at* half past four?

redemittel.p1: Yes, that's fine. What's your name, please?
redemittel.p2: My name is ... Thank you very much. See you on Thursday!

soGehts: Cut page 2 in the middle. Partner A is the customer, Partner B works at the salon.
Read your role card. Don't show it!
Act out the phone call. Say the time aloud; your partner writes it down in numbers.
Write the appointment in the table. Then act out situations 2 and 3.
At the end, compare: did you write down the same appointment?

hinweise: Say "Sorry, could you say that again?" if you don't understand.

schritte.anweisung: Read your role. Phone the salon.
schritte.ziel: You'd like a haircut appointment this week.
infos: You work Monday to Friday from eight until four o'clock.
On Wednesday evening you have an English class.
On Saturday you can only come in the morning.
redemittel: Sorry, could you say that again?
situationen: You phone and make an appointment for yourself.
Your son needs a haircut too. You'd like two appointments, one after the other.
It's Saturday. You are on the bus and you will be 15 minutes late for your appointment at a quarter past ten. Phone the salon.

tipp.beispiel: There _is_ a free appointment *at* half past four.

schritte.anweisung: Read your role. The phone is ringing.
schritte.ziel: You find a free appointment for the customer.
infos: Open: Monday to Friday 9 am-6 pm, Saturday 9 am-1 pm.
Still free: Tuesday 5.30 pm, Thursday 4.30 pm, Saturday 10:15 and 10:45.
A haircut takes 30 minutes and costs £28, for children £15.
situationen: A customer phones and would like an appointment.
The person would like two appointments, one after the other.
The person is late. After their appointment at a quarter past ten, a quarter to eleven is free.

freiFragen: When do you go to the hairdresser's?
When are you free this week? - On ... at ...
What do you do on Saturday at a quarter past ten?

loesungen.antwort: Situation 1: Tuesday at 17:30 (half past five) or Thursday at 16:30 (half past four) or Saturday at 10:15. Wednesday doesn't work (English class), and nothing before 4 pm (work).
Situation 2: Only Saturday works: at 10:15 and at 10:45 (a quarter past ten and a quarter to eleven).
Situation 3: The reception says, for example: No problem, then please come at a quarter to eleven.
